decisive_diff: The 17 C bridge exports are retained. The former Go/CGO bridge is replaced by a native bridge carrying Rust build paths, while the HSM/chai API remains.

ibmkmscrypto platform binaries are replaced by libkpd_hsm_manager 1.0.1. The Go wrapper now embeds the platform library and extracts it atomically to the user cache with SHA-256 verification and 0700 directory / 0755 library modes.
The previous Linux LD_PRELOAD and syscall.Exec workaround is removed. The declared purego dependency changes from 0.10.1 to 0.11.1.

Both Windows releases import CreateFiber, SwitchToFiber, GetThreadContext and SetThreadContext. The old image matches openssl-capi-engine-source-marker, excluding the evasion composite; the new image does not. No executable-memory signature was needed for the alert: its generic injection-directory alternative accepted neutral thread-context pairs.

execution_evidence.behavior: CreateFiber receives fixed callback 0x180058820, zero default stack size and null parameter. This is OpenSSL async job creation, beside ../crypto/async/async.c error diagnostics.
Callback jumps to the OpenSSL async dispatcher, invokes the stored job function, records its return value and returns to the dispatcher fiber through SwitchToFiber.

SuspendThread, WaitForSingleObject(handle,0), GetThreadContext and SetThreadContext set RIP to the fixed cleanup function 0x1804ab080, update pthread cancellation flags, signal an event and resume the thread. This matches MinGW winpthreads pthread_cancel, not an acquired payload or remote process injection.
Cancellation handler walks local cleanup callbacks and exits the thread.
MinGW relocation support queries existing image memory, temporarily adjusts protections and records old protections. This is separate from the OpenSSL fiber callback.

The public bridge initializes the library, calls secsrv_create_session, sets request headers and configures session_http from caller-provided session options. This matches the documented authenticated HSM client purpose.

decoded_strings.assessment: Recovered ordinary HSM field names and runtime/wide strings; no encoded command or secondary payload found.

signature: Current DLL has a verified IBM Authenticode signature, supporting provenance independently of the behavior analysis.
trait_changes: Move fibers-execution out of evasion to the notable fiber-memory-thread-api-profile capability. It establishes API co-occurrence, with no callback-to-memory or remote-handle binding. Preserve original effective PE scope, 50 MiB cap, confidence, alternatives and exclusions.
Move CreateFiber atoms into process/create/fiber; fiber switching, conversion and mixed API-name references into process/fiber. Move the source SwitchToFiber atom out of creation too.

Move nine neutral context pairs/triples into process/info/thread and the suspend/resume pair plus two grouping composites into process/thread/lifecycle. These useful API observations are notable rather than components. Grouping descriptions say thread-control because suspend/resume alone need no context operation.

Update all exact operational consumers. Preserve the former injection-directory alternative in the moved fiber profile by including the relocated two-API group, which covers every relocated pair/triple. No new product exclusion or sample-specific matcher is introduced.

Keep the read/write context-import pair baseline in recognized Go runtime builds, matching its two atoms: the no-op Go fixture contains both imports for routine runtime preemption. This preserves the observable pair rather than suppressing it. The two-API grouping receives the same Go-runtime treatment; ordinary scan output may filter this grouping while validation still checks it.
ancestor_audit: No other operational YAML reference selects the process/thread or process/thread/lifecycle directories. The exact injection/thread-context consumers are updated; the moved fiber profile is the only whole process/inject selector in the operational tree.

Broad process/create selectors gain actual CreateFiber symbol/text observations. This is an intentional correction: fiber creation is execution-context creation. The moved profile requires that same CreateFiber symbol and adds no independent creation population.
The parasitic infector consumer now refers to the neutral fiber API profile with its original matcher population. Its other required VMP/executable-resource evidence and exclusions remain unchanged.

The APC composite uses the toolkit directory as a duplicate-suppression condition. It also explicitly excludes the relocated fiber profile to preserve this behavior. The PowerShell Empire injection-directory selector has PowerShell-only scope and cannot consume the moved PE profile.

Moving the source-only SwitchToFiber call also removes it from broad creation selectors: switching alone does not establish context creation. The combined RWX fiber callback composite and exact Empire source consumer retain their explicit switch requirement.

validation.focused_controls: Six cases: five inert PE64 import-table controls plus the repository no-op Go executable (statically scanned, never executed). Ordinary custom API sets remain notable; the Go runtime pair remains baseline. All controls require zero suspicious/hostile findings.
